knee-ex-1.title: Quadriceps Sets
knee-ex-1.description: An isometric exercise to activate the quadriceps muscles without stressing the knee joint.
instructions: Sit or lie down with your leg extended.
Tighten the muscle on the top of your thigh.
Press the back of your knee gently down toward the floor.
Hold the contraction for 5 seconds.
Relax and repeat.
knee-ex-1.safety: Stop if you feel sharp pain. Focus on gentle isometric activation only.

knee-ex-2.title: Straight Leg Raises
knee-ex-2.description: Strengthens the quadriceps and hip flexors while keeping the knee in extension.
instructions: Lie on your back with the non-injured knee bent.
Keep the injured leg straight and tighten the thigh muscle.
Lift the straight leg to the height of the bent knee.
Hold for 3 seconds at the top.
Slowly lower back to the floor.
knee-ex-2.safety: Keep your core engaged. Do not hold your breath.

knee-ex-3.title: Heel Slides
knee-ex-3.description: Gentle range-of-motion exercise to restore knee flexion gradually.
instructions: Lie on your back with both legs extended.
Slowly slide your heel toward your buttocks, bending the knee.
Slide only as far as is comfortable.
Hold the bent position for 5 seconds.
Slide your heel back to the starting position.
knee-ex-3.safety: Never force the range. Work within a pain-free arc only.

knee-ex-4.title: Mini Squats
knee-ex-4.description: Functional strengthening exercise to build quadriceps strength in a closed-chain position.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding a sturdy surface.
Slowly bend your knees as if sitting in a chair.
Go down only 30–45 degrees (one-quarter squat).
Hold for 3 seconds at the bottom.
Slowly stand back up, squeezing the glutes.
knee-ex-4.safety: Do not let the knee cave inward. Use a mirror for alignment feedback.

knee-ex-5.title: Terminal Knee Extension (Band)
knee-ex-5.description: Targets the VMO (vastus medialis oblique) for medial knee stability.
instructions: Attach a resistance band to a fixed object and around your knee.
Stand with the band creating tension behind the knee.
Lock out the knee by tightening the quadriceps.
Hold for 3 seconds in full extension.
Slowly return to slight knee bend.
knee-ex-5.safety: Avoid hyperextending the knee. Begin with light resistance.

knee-ex-6.title: Step-Ups
knee-ex-6.description: Advanced functional exercise integrating strength, balance, and coordination.
instructions: Stand in front of a sturdy 6-inch step.
Step up with the injured leg, keeping the knee aligned over the toe.
Push through the heel to fully stand on the step.
Slowly lower the other leg back down.
Repeat by alternating legs.
knee-ex-6.safety: Avoid letting the knee buckle inward when stepping up or down.

leg-ex-1.title: Standing Calf Raises
leg-ex-1.description: Builds calf strength and ankle stability for walking and balance.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding a chair for support.
Slowly rise up onto the balls of your feet.
Hold the top position for 2 seconds.
Lower the heels back to the floor with control.
leg-ex-1.safety: Keep the movement slow and controlled. Avoid bouncing at the bottom.

leg-ex-2.title: Clamshells
leg-ex-2.description: Activates the hip abductors and external rotators for pelvic stability.
instructions: Lie on your side with knees bent at 45 degrees.
Keep feet together as you lift the top knee upward.
Hold for 2 seconds at the top.
Slowly lower back to the starting position.
leg-ex-2.safety: Do not roll the pelvis backward. Keep the top hip stacked over the bottom.

leg-ex-3.title: Glute Bridges
leg-ex-3.description: Strengthens the gluteus maximus and hamstrings while protecting the lower back.
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Squeeze your glutes and lift your hips off the floor.
Hold for 3 seconds at the top.
Slowly lower back down.
leg-ex-3.safety: Keep the pelvis flat. Avoid excessive lumbar extension.

leg-ex-4.title: Step-Ups (Hip Focus)
leg-ex-4.description: Functional unilateral exercise for hip strength and balance.
instructions: Stand in front of a 6-inch step.
Step up by driving through the heel and engaging the glutes.
Briefly stand tall on the step.
Slowly step back down with control.
leg-ex-4.safety: Avoid letting the knee drift medially. Engage glutes at the top.

leg-ex-5.title: Single-Leg Balance
leg-ex-5.description: Improves proprioception, ankle stability, and balance reactions.
instructions: Stand near a wall or chair for safety.
Lift one foot slightly off the floor.
Hold the single-leg stance for 30 seconds.
Switch legs and repeat.
leg-ex-5.safety: Stay close to a wall. Discontinue immediately if you feel unsafe.

leg-ex-6.title: Lateral Band Walks
leg-ex-6.description: Targets hip abductors for stability during walking and athletic motion.
instructions: Place a resistance band around your thighs, just above the knees.
Stand with feet hip-width apart and slight knee bend.
Step sideways with one foot, then bring the other foot in slightly.
Continue for the prescribed distance, then switch directions.
leg-ex-6.safety: Keep the band taut throughout. Do not let the knees collapse inward.

elbow-ex-1.title: Elbow Flexion & Extension
elbow-ex-1.description: Restores basic elbow range of motion in a pain-free arc.
instructions: Sit with the arm supported on a table or your thigh.
Slowly bend the elbow as far as comfort allows.
Pause for 2 seconds at end range.
Slowly straighten the elbow back to neutral.
elbow-ex-1.safety: Work within a pain-free range only. Do not force the end range.

elbow-ex-2.title: Wrist Curls
elbow-ex-2.description: Strengthens the wrist flexors to support elbow function.
instructions: Rest your forearm on a table, palm facing up.
Hold a light dumbbell in your hand.
Curl the wrist up as high as possible.
Slowly lower back to the starting position.
elbow-ex-2.safety: Use very light resistance. Avoid clenching the fist tightly.

elbow-ex-3.title: Forearm Pronation / Supination
elbow-ex-3.description: Restores rotational range of the forearm.
instructions: Hold a light hammer or small dumbbell in your hand.
Rest the elbow on a table at 90 degrees, knuckles facing up.
Slowly rotate the palm down (pronate), then up (supinate).
Move only through a comfortable range.
elbow-ex-3.safety: Slow and controlled. Resistance should be very light.

elbow-ex-4.title: Bicep Curls (Light)
elbow-ex-4.description: Rebuilds bicep strength with a controlled curl.
instructions: Stand with arms by your side, holding a light dumbbell.
Curl the dumbbell upward, keeping the elbow at your side.
Pause at the top.
Slowly lower back down with control.
elbow-ex-4.safety: Keep the upper arm stationary. Don't swing the body.

elbow-ex-5.title: Tricep Extensions
elbow-ex-5.description: Strengthens the triceps for elbow extension.
instructions: Sit or stand and hold a light dumbbell with both hands behind your head.
Slowly straighten your arms by extending the elbows.
Pause briefly at full extension.
Lower back with control.
elbow-ex-5.safety: Avoid locking out the elbows under heavy load. Keep the core engaged.

elbow-ex-6.title: Eccentric Wrist Extensions
elbow-ex-6.description: Targets the wrist extensors with a slow eccentric load — useful for tennis elbow.
instructions: Rest your forearm on a table, palm facing down.
Use the opposite hand to lift the dumbbell up.
Slowly lower the dumbbell over 3–5 seconds.
Repeat for the prescribed reps.
elbow-ex-6.safety: Lower very slowly. Stop if symptoms worsen.
